evidence: src/infrastructure/composition/AppFactory.ts: createApp() is the only place that creates concrete adapters (InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository, InMemoryTaskRepository, UuidIdGenerator). src/infrastructure/composition/Dependencies.ts: `export interface Dependencies { users; projects; tasks; ids }` is the shared contract, typed against the UserRepository/ProjectRepository/TaskRepository interfaces and the IdGenerator port.

src/infrastructure/composition/ProjectModule.ts: createProjectRoutes(deps: Dependencies) builds CreateProjectUseCase, CreateTaskUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase using only deps.projects/deps.tasks/deps.ids.

src/infrastructure/composition/TaskModule.ts: createTaskRoutes(deps: Dependencies) builds AssignTaskUseCase(deps.tasks, deps.users) and CompleteTaskUseCase(deps.tasks). It creates no adapters of its own.
src/infrastructure/composition/UserModule.ts: createUserRoutes(deps: Dependencies) builds CreateUserUseCase(deps.users, deps.ids), following the same factory shape as the other feature modules.
Each use case is created in exactly one feature module, so no wiring rule is duplicated.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module passes. All five files share one job: composing the application. AppFactory.ts builds the shared adapters into a single Dependencies object, creates the express app and mounts each feature's routes. Dependencies.ts declares the shared adapter contract, typed against the domain repository and application port interfaces. ProjectModule.ts, TaskModule.ts and UserModule.ts each do the same narrow thing: take `deps: Dependencies`, build their use cases, inject them into a controller and return its routes. All three feature modules read adapters only through the Dependencies abstraction. None of them builds a concrete adapter of its own, so the module never bypasses its own abstractions. Concrete adapters are created in exactly one place (createApp), so each wiring decision lives in one place. Each use case is created once: CreateTaskUseCase appears only in ProjectModule, under the project routes, and is not duplicated in TaskModule. No unrelated concern is mixed in. Import direction is out of scope and was not judged.
